# Exact cap-incidence circulation for a simultaneous convex partition

Use the actual simultaneous partition in
`candidate edf02845b3275e8c`. Its positive-mass
cells D_i are winner regions of affine scores

    L_i(z,x)=beta_i+b_i.z+u_i.x,
    D_i=C intersect {L_i>=L_k for all k}.             (1)

The pairwise continuous score differences are nonconstant on every
positive intrinsic fiber, so ties have zero mixed measure. Write

    t_i=mu(D_i)>0,
    y_i=(j_i,c_i)=(1/t_i) integral_(D_i)(z,x) dmu.

Here j_i is integer when integer base moments were prescribed. There may
be at most 2^n cells by the proved minimum-base-variance compression, but
the identities below hold for any finite positive class family. They
retain the original source cells and all source moments.

The new conclusion is a strict directed-cycle identity for the dual caps,
with an EXACT integer-tilt correction for other caps of the same continuous
normals. A rectangle calibration proves that neither the strict identity
nor acyclicity alone gives the needed depth bound. Averaging positive
continuous-normal circuits does not remove the correction by virtue of
the known first moments; Section 4 makes the surviving term explicit.

## 1. The strict source-integral gap

For k!=i define

    Delta_(k,i)=L_k(y_k)-L_i(y_k)
       =(1/t_k) integral_(D_k)(L_k-L_i) dmu.         (2)

The integrand is nonnegative on D_k and strictly positive almost
everywhere there, by the null-tie property. Since t_k>0,

    Delta_(k,i)>0.                                  (3)

This proof uses actual cell membership, not just a separation of the
target bases. In particular each true cell centroid lies strictly on its
own side of every pairwise score boundary, even when it lies on the
boundary of the original ambient C.

Center the score at its own centroid:

    ell_i(z,x)=L_i(z,x)-L_i(y_i)
               =b_i.(z-j_i)+u_i.(x-c_i).             (4)

When the score is nonconstant, {ell_i>=0} is an actual closed halfspace
through y_i. One may prescribe all u_i nonzero when constructing the
partition. Constant-score cases can simply be read as affine superlevel
sets; none is used in the examples below.

Let alpha_(i,k)>=0, with alpha_(i,i)=0, be a circulation on the class
labels, meaning

    sum_k alpha_(i,k)=sum_k alpha_(k,i) for every i.

The exact identity is

    sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k) ell_i(y_k)
       =-sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k) Delta_(k,i).           (5)

Indeed ell_i(y_k)=L_k(y_k)-L_i(y_i)-Delta_(k,i), and the first two
terms cancel after summation precisely by the circulation condition.
The right side is strictly negative for any nonzero off-diagonal
circulation.

In particular the directed graph

    i -> k  iff i!=k and ell_i(y_k)>=0

has no directed cycle. A cycle's incidence weights would contradict (5).
Equivalently, no directed cycle of these original dual caps can capture
all of its next centroids, even with all boundary points included. The
strict deficit in (5) is the sum of the actual normalized cell integrals
in (2), not a combinatorial sign assigned independently of the source.

## 2. The necessary integer-tilt correction

Consider instead arbitrary actual cap margins through the same centers,
with the SAME continuous coefficients as their respective scores:

    h_i(z,x)=a_i.(z-j_i)+u_i.(x-c_i).

Then h_i=ell_i+(a_i-b_i).(z-j_i), so (5) becomes

    sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k) h_i(y_k)
      =-sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k) Delta_(k,i)
        +sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k)(a_i-b_i).(j_k-j_i).   (6)

If every edge with positive weight captures its destination centroid,
the final integer circulation must therefore pay the strict source gap:

    sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k)(a_i-b_i).(j_k-j_i)
        >=sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k) Delta_(k,i)>0.         (7)

The cell constraints integral_(D_i)(z-j_i)dmu=0 concern each cell's own
source. They do not set this different cross-center circulation to zero.
No equality between the source score coefficient b_i and a depth cap's
integer coefficient a_i is implicit in the simultaneous realization.

For completely arbitrary continuous coefficients v_i, the same calculation
has the further, equally necessary term

    sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k)(v_i-u_i).(c_k-c_i).         (8)

Thus replacing a cap direction by a score direction cannot be done
silently either. Positive rescalings of cap margins must be tracked
before comparing their coefficients; (6) uses the displayed scaling.

## 3. Exact actual-source calibration and two limits of the identity

Take C=[-1,2]x[0,1], its four unit integer fibers, and scores

    L_0=3/5-z/5-x,   L_1=x+z/5-3/5.

Their winner cells are the minimum-base-variance partition from
`candidate b5f24b03b630e2b0`.
Their masses and centroids are

    t_0=t_1=2,  y_0=(0,3/10), y_1=(1,7/10).

Both own score values are 3/10; the two cross-score values are -3/10.
Consequently

    Delta_(0,1)=Delta_(1,0)=3/5.

The centered DUAL caps themselves are

    ell_0=3/10-x-z/5>=0,
    ell_1=x+z/5-9/10>=0.                            (9)

Their fiber mass lists, at z=-1,0,1,2, are respectively

    (1/2,3/10,1/10,0),
    (0,1/10,3/10,1/2).

Each has total mass 9/10<M/4=1. Each cap is entirely inside its own winner
cell on C, so it has zero outside-piece source mass. The cross-centroid
values are both -3/5, and their cycle sum is exactly -6/5, as required by
(5). Thus even matching the bad caps to the actual dual integer scores,
and retaining a strictly positive source gap, does not make either cell
centroid deep. Acyclicity is a genuine incidence constraint, not a depth
selection theorem or an automatic cross-capture mechanism.

To see exactly why the integer correction cannot be omitted, retain the
same source and centers but change the cap tilts to

    h_0=3/10-x+z/2,
    h_1=x-7/10-(z-1)/2.

Now h_0(y_1)=h_1(y_0)=1/10, so there IS a two-cycle. Here

    a_0-b_0=7/10,   a_1-b_1=-7/10,
    integer cycle term=7/5,
    -6/5+7/5=1/5.                                  (10)

Both new caps have mass 21/10; their sum margin is 1/10, so they cover
the full ambient space. They are not low-budget caps. This example
refutes cancellation based solely on actual source moments and scores;
it does not refute a proposed estimate that additionally and explicitly
uses a below-OC cap budget.

## 4. What positive normal circuits cancel, and what they do not

Suppose that at each center i there is a finite family of cap margins

    h_(i,r)(z,x)=a_(i,r).(z-j_i)+v_(i,r).(x-c_i),

with rho_(i,r)>=0, sum_r rho_(i,r)=1, and

    sum_r rho_(i,r) v_(i,r)=0.

No such balanced low-budget circuit is inferred from an arbitrary bad
centroid; this paragraph states its consequence IF the family is given.
Set A_i=sum_r rho_(i,r)a_(i,r). Then, identically at every point,

    sum_r rho_(i,r)h_(i,r)(z,x)=A_i.(z-j_i).

For any circulation alpha this yields

    sum_(i,k,r) alpha_(i,k)rho_(i,r)h_(i,r)(y_k)
        =sum_(i,k) alpha_(i,k)A_i.(j_k-j_i).          (11)

Applying (6)--(8) before averaging gives exactly the same answer. The
continuous correction averages to -u_i.(c_k-c_i); together with the
integer -b_i term it cancels the entire strict dual-score gap in (5).
Thus the score gap has not survived as an extra negative term in (11).
The remaining integer circulation is not known to vanish.

An actual-source example excludes deriving that vanishing from the
known first moments and positive normal balance alone. Keep the same
rectangle partition and define two caps per center with

    v_(i,+)=1, v_(i,-)=-1, rho_(i,+)=rho_(i,-)=1/2,
    a_(0,+)=a_(0,-)=1/2,
    a_(1,+)=a_(1,-)=-1/2.

Each group is a genuine positive continuous-normal circuit whose caps
cover the entire continuous fiber over its own integer center. All own
source first moments of these through-centroid margins are zero. Yet
for the two-cycle alpha_(0,1)=alpha_(1,0)=1, the right side of (11) is

    (1/2)(1-0)+(-1/2)(0-1)=1,                       (12)

not zero. Its four cap masses are 29/10,21/10,21/10,29/10, so again this
is an exact obstruction to moment-only cancellation, not a low-budget
endpoint counterexample.

## 5. Scope and dependencies

The partition's finite-score attainment, actual source moments, and
null-tie property are supplied by the proved simultaneous-partition
theorem. Equations (2)--(12) then follow from affine integration and
finite sums, with no localization, regularity, or mixed centroid-depth
assumption. The rectangle is an actual convex body throughout.

The new retained information is the strict cell-integral circulation
gap together with its necessary continuous and integer corrections.
Turning it into a global low-cap-budget estimate still requires an
additional proved bound on those corrections. The already disproved
continuous gamma bound for each mixed piece, positive outside-piece
compensation, and minimum-base-variance centroid selector are not used.
